decision:
Merged. The structure and the way changes are made come from B; the measurements and the mark details come from A.

What was taken, and why:
1. **One area at a time, each with its own address (B), and no separate home page.** A's sticky index with live summaries becomes a local nav column (208 px) that stays beside the area on desktop. Settings therefore opens straight on Team, with all four summaries in view. On phones the same nav is the landing list, and an area opens full screen with a back link (B's list, then detail).
   - Reason: the four areas do different jobs (people, messages, identity, money). Shown one at a time, each gets one H2, one primary action and one scope. That is calmer than A's 3,100 px page of four forms, and the summaries still give A's at-a-glance status.
2. **Every setting changes on its own and is confirmed by an inline note with Undo (B).** This replaces A's per-part forms, changed-field rules, sticky save bars, blocked states and Ctrl/Cmd S.
   - It is the app's own pattern: the Line's 8 s Undo note, Today's "Take it back", and principle 2 in PRODUCT.md ("a handoff can be taken back").
   - It needs no dirty-form machinery.
   - At 375 px, A's index, save bar and tab bar together would cover about 176 of 812 px.
3. **Channels start honest (B): Email on, WhatsApp and SMS not connected, with a simulated Connect.**
   - Build seeds `channel: 'Email'` on every step of Sufra's line and offers "By" only on Send blocks (build.js lines 42 and 254). A's three WhatsApp steps would contradict another screen of the same prototype.
   - A connected WhatsApp would also present a live integration, which guidelines rule 10 forbids.
4. **Who does a step stays a property of the versioned line (B's removal guard).** A's rule "Reem's steps go to Hala" would edit version 3 from Settings, outside draft and publish.
5. **Two roles, Owner and Member (A).** They match the two kinds of users in PRODUCT.md. B's Manager role and its table would be a new product decision with no evidence behind it.
6. **Billing stays plain (A: "None yet", no card form), with B's brackets for plan and price.** A's "Pilot" plan and B's paid invoices with [AMOUNT] are invented facts.
7. **Also kept:**
   - From A: the 192 px logo rule (twice the 96 px mark sign-up draws), the 136 px sidebar name box, previews at true sizes, the dashed grey loop for "not saved yet" turning into a solid violet loop when saved, and the 08:00 to 18:00 hours that order.js, overview.js and today.js already draw.
   - From B: the invitation drawn as a sent straight plus a waiting arch (Nour accepting rewrites the arch as a loop), the mark explained on ink in the tile's own palette, the messages on the line with today's real sends, the preview filled from a real job, and iconOf splitting on '#'.

Claims checked in the code and in the browser:
- jobs.js `strip()` always draws a train and draws the branch dip only for a job on the branch, so a strip with rings and no train is new. Both were right.
- grammar.js `lead()` is private. Both were right.
- In sufra.js, people have no email or access, and there are no invite, org, channel or billing records. Both were right.
- order.js writes client links as sufra.iqaa.app/q/{last four}. B was right; system.html's /r/… is an identity example.
- app.js `iconOf` splits only on '?'. B was right. New finding: the search dialog stays open when a result only changes the hash, so it must close first.
- main is 1,173.6 px at 1440. A was right.
- The sidebar name box is 136 px, which holds about 17 letters of 15 px bold (measured average 7.87 px). B's 17 is closer than A's 18.
- The four area names take 207.6 px at 14 px. A was right.
- The phone tab bar is 359 px for items of at least 64 px, so it holds 5. A was right.
- Contrast on white: n700 8.16:1, n600 5.65:1, n500 3.95:1, violet 4.94:1. B's 8.3 and 5.9 were slightly high.
- `--m-bar` (2400 ms) is "the longest anything may take". A was right, but that limit is for animation, not reading time, so notes stay 8 s as on the Line.

Watch-outs:
- `NAV`, `NEXT`, `PAGES`, `SCREENS` and sufra.js are shared with the Clients and Ask Watar builds, so every addition must be additive.
- The Line and Build do not check roles yet.
- Which way each message goes lives both in Build's seed and in SUFRA.messages. Keep both on Email until Build reads SUFRA.messages.
pages: settings.html: desktop (viewport 900 px or wider) opens on Team; a phone (narrower than 900 px) opens on the list of the four areas.

settings.html#team, settings.html#channels, settings.html#organization, settings.html#billing: one area each, with its own document title (for example 'Team · Settings · Sufra'). Back and forward move between them.
settings.html?as=reem (also salma or yusuf): the same page seen by a member, read-only, with Billing locked. It combines with a hash, for example settings.html?as=reem#billing.
settings.html?as=hala, or no ?as=: Hala, the owner (the default).
Any other hash shows the default view. #main (the skip link) keeps the current view. Area sections use ids se-team … so a hash never matches an element and the browser never jumps on its own.
layout_desktop:
**Frame.** Unchanged: the lavender desk, the 248 px sidebar with Settings current, and the white sheet (16 px radius). At 1440 × 900, main measures 1,173.6 px and .ap-wrap (32 px gutters) leaves 1,109.6 px.

**Head (.se-head).** Padding-block 32 / 24, as on Orders.
- H1 'Settings' at 31/44, −0.015em.
- Lead at 16/24 in n700, max 64ch.
- No buttons and no mark: the sidebar already shows Sufra's mark at 32 px.

**Body.** .se-body is an inline-size container holding .se-grid.
- Content of 960 px or more (1280 px and up with the sidebar open, about 1104 px and up with it folded): a grid of 208 px | minmax(0, 1fr) with a 48 px column gap. The area column is capped at 880 px, which gives 853.6 px at 1440 and 704 px at 1280. Rows never stretch when the sidebar folds.
- Content under 960 px (windows of 900 to 1279 px): the nav becomes one row of four links above the area. Each link is 44 px tall at 15 px, the current one bold on n100 with a 10 px radius. overflow-x: auto is a fallback. Summaries are hidden, and the area takes the full width.

**Local nav (.se-nav).** Sticky 24 px from the top.
- Four links, 4 px apart, each at least 56 px tall, with padding 10 / 12 and a 10 px radius.
- Name at 15/20, weight 600. Summary at 13/18 in n700. Organization's summary is a 20 px mark followed by sufra.iqaa.app in Fragment Mono 12/18.
- Current: n100 ground and the name at 700. This is the app's own current-state convention (the Orders tabs, the phone tab bar). Hover: n50.

**Area head (.se-ahd).**
- H2 at 20/32, weight 700. That is two steps of the 1.25 scale under the H1 and two above the 16 px body, so the four areas read as peers.
- Description at 15/22 in n700, max 64ch.
- The area's one head action at the end of the row (Team: 'Invite someone').
- 24 px under the head.

**Team (853.6 px).**
- A quiet label row at 12/16, 700, n600: Person · On the line · Waiting now · Role (aria-hidden).
- People rows on minmax(0,1.6fr) minmax(0,1.5fr) minmax(0,0.8fr) minmax(0,0.6fr) 64px, column gap 24, padding 16 / 12, at least 80 px tall, with n100 hairlines between them. This is the Orders rhythm: no cards, no row hover.
  - Who: the 32 px lilac avatar (.me-av), the name at 16/22, 700, then 'What they do · email' at 13/20 in n700.
  - On the line: the 150 × 26 strip, then words at 13/20 in n700.
  - Waiting now: a link whose count is in Fragment Mono 14.
  - Role: 15/22.
  - Edit: a 44 px text button.
- An open editor sits under its row: an n50 block, 16 px radius, padding 20 / 24, in two columns (fields up to 400 px | Their steps on the line) with a 32 px gap.
- Under the list, the coverage sentence at 13/20 in n700.
- Then H3 'Invited' at 15/22, 700, 32 px above, with the invitation rows on the same grid.
- At 1440 × 900 the head, four people and Nour take about 770 px, so they fit on one screen.

**Channels.** A grid of minmax(0,1fr) | 320 px, gap 40.
- Left column:
  - H3 'Ways to reach clients' and three two-line rows. Line 1: name at 16/22, 700, the state at 15, and the action at the end. Line 2: the detail at 13/20 in n700.
  - H3 'Messages on the line', its caption, and six two-line rows. Line 1: a 24 px glyph, the step at 15/22, 700, and today's event at the end in Fragment Mono 13. Line 2: 'Quote · to the client · by email' at 13/20 in n700. Each row is a button with a 12 px radius, n50 on hover and n100 while pressed.
- Right column: H3 'What the client gets' and the preview, sticky 24 px from the top. It is about 470 px tall, so it fits a 900 px viewport. The email frame is white with a 1 px n200 ring and a 12 px radius. It is the one framed object on the page, because an email is a framed thing.
- Below a 680 px area, the preview drops under the lists and stops sticking.

**Organization.** Grid areas 'rows mark' / 'rows where', columns minmax(0,1fr) | 320 px, gap 40.
- Setting rows: label at 14/20, 700; value at 16/24 (Fragment Mono for the address and the times); hint at 13/20 in n700; Change at the end. Each row is at least 72 px tall, with n100 hairlines.
- Mark panel: H3, the two radios, then the ink plate (16 px radius, padding 16) with the 96 px mark and the opening legend, then the caption.
- Where it appears: snippets at true size, each on its real ground (the sidebar on n100, the others white with a 1 px n200 ring and a 12 px radius). With the plate, these are the only rounded grounds on the page, because they show other places.
- Below 680 px it becomes one column, in the order mark, rows, where.

**Billing.** One column, max 640 px, using the same setting rows plus a definition list with its numbers in Fragment Mono.

**Notes.** Each note sits inline in its own row (14/20, a 16 px loop glyph, Undo as a link). There is no toast and no bar.

**Shadows.** None new.
layout_mobile:
**Frame.** The phone frame is unchanged: a static top bar (Sufra's mark, name, menu and search) and the fixed tab bar (Overview, Today, Line, Orders).
- Settings never takes a tab. The bar is 359 px wide for items of at least 64 px, so it holds five, and Clients and Ask Watar are coming.
- The ways in are the organization menu's 'Settings' and search.

**List view (settings.html with no hash).** 16 px gutters.
- H1 at 25/36; lead at 15/22 in n700.
- The four areas as full-width rows. The whole row is one link, at least 72 px tall, padding 14 / 0, with n100 hairlines.
  - Name at 16/24, 700.
  - Summary at 14/20 in n700, or the 16 px dashed grey loop with 'Not saved yet'.
  - A 10 px chevron in n500 at the inline end.
- The head and the four rows end at about 470 px.

**Area view (#team, #channels, #organization, #billing).**
- A 44 px '← Settings' link (15/20, 600) at the top. The H1 stays in the DOM but is visually hidden. The H2 is 25/36, because it is the page title here. Description at 15/22. Content in one column.
- Team:
  - Rows stack (the list container is under 680 px). Line 1: avatar, name, what they do, email, and the role at the end. Line 2: the 150 px strip and its words. Line 3: the waiting link and Edit, both 44 px tall.
  - The editor opens in place at full width, fields first, then 'Their steps on the line'. Save comes first at full width (the existing .row-act rule under 600 px).
  - The invite form stacks its fields.
- Channels: the ways rows wrap their action under the detail. Message rows keep two lines, with today's event moving to line 2. The preview follows the lists at full width (343 px at most) and does not stick.
- Organization: the mark panel comes first (the plate with a 72 px mark and the legend beside it, the caption under it), then the rows, then 'Where it appears' in one column. The 224 px sidebar snippet fits inside 343 px.
- Billing: rows.
- Notes wrap under their row's value.

**Space and overflow.**
- app.css already pads the page for the 68 px tab bar. There are no sticky bars on this page, so nothing else covers content.
- No horizontal scroll: the widest fixed pieces are the 224 px sidebar snippet and the 150 px strips.

sections.name: Frame, routing and ways in
sections.content:
**Page.** settings.html is written by tools/p_settings.py: shell('se', 'Settings · Sufra', app_top('Settings'), body, ('sufra', 'jobs', 'settings'), foot, css=('app', 'settings')). main.se is a white sheet.

**Static skeleton** (rendered by Python):
- the head;
- the nav with four links;
- four sections (ids se-team, se-channels, se-organization, se-billing), each with its H2 (tabindex -1) and description;
- one visually hidden polite live region;
- <template data-runs> holding the Runs on Iqaa badge as a span (runs_badge() with <a> turned into <span>);
- <template data-lock> holding icon('Lock', 18).

assets/js/settings.js renders everything else.

**Ways in.**
- Sidebar: Settings leaves 'Coming next' and becomes the last link of the main list, with aria-current on this page. Its <li class="ap-wide"> is hidden in the phone tab bar.
- Organization menu: the disabled 'Organization settings · Soon' becomes a link 'Settings' (Settings icon, 18 px) to settings.html.
- Search (Ctrl/Cmd K) gets five results:
  - Settings: 'Team, channels, the organization and its mark, billing'
  - Team: 'People and roles; invite someone' (#team)
  - Channels: 'Email, WhatsApp and SMS' (#channels)
  - Organization: 'Name, address, hours, mark and logo' (#organization)
  - Billing: 'Plan and what Sufra uses' (#billing)

sections.name: Head
sections.content:
- H1: 'Settings'.
- Lead: 'How Sufra is set up. Each change applies on its own, and you can take it back.'
- For a member, the lead reads: 'You can see how Sufra is set up. Owners change it: ask Hala.'
sections.interactions: None. The organization name in titles and notes follows a saved rename.

sections.name: Local nav: the four areas and their state
sections.content:
nav aria-label 'Settings areas', with four links in the brief's order. Each summary is computed from saved state only:
- Team: '4 people · 1 invited'
- Channels: 'Sends by email'. Once WhatsApp is connected: 'Email and WhatsApp on'. With all three: 'Email, WhatsApp and SMS on'.
- Organization: Sufra's mark at 20 px (the grammar holds the pen at 1.5 px), then 'sufra.iqaa.app' in Fragment Mono.
- Billing: '[PLAN] · [PRICE] a month'. For a member: 'Owners only'.

While an area holds an open editor whose values differ from the saved ones, its summary becomes a 16 px dashed grey loop and 'Not saved yet'.
sections.interactions:
- A press routes to the area. The open area carries aria-current='page'.
- Summaries change only after a save or an Undo.
- 'Not saved yet' appears on the first changed keystroke and leaves on Save or Cancel.
- Accessible names include the summary: 'Team, 4 people, 1 invited' or 'Team, not saved yet'.

sections.name: How a change is made (every area)
sections.interactions:
- Escape in an editor works as Cancel: drafts are dropped and focus returns to the action.
- Enter in a one-line field submits its editor.
- Typed values live in state.drafts[editorId]:
  - redrawing a list never drops typing;
  - an editor left open with changes is still there after visiting another area, and the nav says 'Not saved yet'.
- Opening an editor closes any other unchanged editor in the same area. Changed editors stay open.
- beforeunload warns only while some editor holds unsaved changes.
- On Save, the pen writes the note's loop in a quarter beat (Beats.write). With reduced motion the loop simply appears.
- Errors use sign-up's .err under the field, with aria-invalid and aria-describedby. Save moves focus to the first invalid field.

sections.name: Team: people
sections.content:
- **H2:** 'Team'.
- **Description:** 'Who signs in at sufra.iqaa.app, what they do on the line and what they can change. Clients never need an account: they answer from a link.'
- **Head action:** 'Invite someone' (.btn.primary).

**Rows**, in the order a job meets each person:
- Reem · Quotes and new orders · reem@sufra.example
  - Strip ringed at Request and Quote; 'Request, Quote · 3 steps'
  - '3 jobs' → today.html?as=reem
  - Member · Edit
- Hala (you) · Owner, buying · hala@sufra.example
  - Strip ringed at Buy materials and, on the branch dip, Wholesale order; 'Buy materials, Wholesale order · 2 steps'
  - '1 job' → today.html?as=hala
  - Owner · Edit
- Salma · Kitchen · salma@sufra.example
  - Strip ringed at Prepare; 'Prepare · 1 step'
  - '1 job' → today.html?as=salma
  - Member · Edit
- Yusuf · Delivery · yusuf@sufra.example
  - Strip ringed at Deliver; 'Deliver · 1 step'
  - '1 job' → today.html?as=yusuf
  - Member · Edit

**Under the list:** 'Every step a person does on the line has someone: 7 are the team’s, 1 is the client’s.'

**Strip:** JOBS.on(line).reach(ring). It is Today's and Orders' strip without a train: the person's stations are ringed violet, and the branch dip is drawn only when a ringed station is on it.
sections.interactions:
- **Waiting link.** '3 jobs' is a link (aria-label '3 jobs wait on Reem now. Open Reem’s Today.'), as on Overview's team list. It reads 'None now' when nothing waits.
- **Edit** is a disclosure (aria-expanded, aria-controls) that opens the person's editor under the row.
- Rows are not links and have no hover.

sections.name: Team: a person's editor and the removal guard
sections.content:
Two columns on wide screens, one on narrow ones.

**What they do.** A required text field, up to 40 characters. Hint: 'Shown beside their name on Overview and Today.'

**Role.** A fieldset with legend 'Role' and two radios, each with a description:
- Owner: 'Changes, tests and publishes the line, invites people, changes these settings and sees billing.'
- Member: 'Does the steps the line gives them, and sees every order and client.'

In your own editor the role is text: 'Owner. Another owner can change your role.'

**Their steps on the line.** One line per step: its glyph, then the step and its station, with the jobs at that step now as links under it. For Reem:
- loop · 'Reem logs the order · Request'
- arch · 'Approves Watar’s draft of the quote · Quote', now: Lunch for Nakhla (SFR-26-0031), Board breakfast (SFR-26-0034)
- loop · 'Reem checks the prices · Quote', now: Graduation dinner (SFR-26-0032)

Then the link 'Change who does a step, on the Line' (line.html).

**Remove {name} from Sufra.** A text button that is aria-disabled while the person has a step on the line or a job waiting. The reason is written beside it:
- 'Reem does 3 steps at Request and Quote, and 3 jobs wait on Reem now. Give these steps to someone else on the Line first.'
- 'Yusuf does 1 step at Deliver, and 1 job waits on Yusuf now. Give this step to someone else on the Line first.'

It is not shown in your own editor.

**Buttons:** Cancel / Save.
sections.interactions:
- **Save** applies What they do and Role. Notes: 'Saved: Salma is an owner now.' and 'Saved: Salma now does ‘Kitchen lead’.', each with Undo.
- **Remove** is allowed only for someone with no steps and no waiting jobs; in the demo that is Nour once she has joined. It removes the row at once and leaves 'Nour is no longer on Sufra’s team.' with Undo.
- **Who does a step is never changed here.** The line has versions, so its steps are edited and published on the Line and in Build.

sections.name: Team: invitations
sections.content:
**H3 'Invited'** sits under the people.

**Nour's row:**
- An empty 32 px avatar: a 1.5 px n500 ring with N in n700.
- The invitation drawn as one short line, an ink straight then a violet arch (IQ.line([['run','held']], { k: 0.75 }) inside an aria-hidden span), with: 'Waiting for Nour to accept · sent Fri 30 Oct, 16:20 by Hala · the link works until Fri 6 Nov'.
- Member.
- Actions: 'Send again' and 'Cancel the invitation'.

With no invitations: 'No invitations out.'

**Invite form**, opened by 'Invite someone': an n50 block with a 16 px radius at the top of the people list.
- H3: 'Invite someone to Sufra'.
- Fields:
  - Name;
  - Work email (inputmode email);
  - What they do (placeholder 'For example: kitchen, delivery');
  - Role radios, with Member checked.
- Hint: 'Iqaa emails them a link to join Sufra. It works for seven days.'
- Buttons: Cancel / 'Send the invitation' (violet).
sections.interactions:
- **Validation messages:**
  - 'Write their name.'
  - 'Enter their work email.'
  - 'That doesn’t look like an email address. Check for a missing @ or dot.' (sign-up's EMAIL rule and words)
  - 'reem@sufra.example already belongs to Reem.'
  - 'Nour already has an invitation from Fri 30 Oct. Send it again instead.'
- **Send:**
  - a new row appears in Invited;
  - the pen writes its straight, then its arch, a quarter beat each;
  - the row reads 'sent just now by Hala · the link works until Sun 8 Nov';
  - note: 'Invitation to Rana is ready. In this prototype nothing is sent.' with Undo.
- **Send again:** 'sent again just now · the link works until Sun 8 Nov', with a note and Undo.
- **Cancel the invitation:** a placeholder 'Nour’s invitation is cancelled.' with Undo.
- **Footer control 'Let Nour accept her invitation'**, shown only while her invitation is pending:
  - the pen rewrites her line as a straight, then a loop, a quarter beat a stroke: the approval moment from the Motion page;
  - after half a beat her row moves into the people list as 'Nour · Kitchen · nour@sufra.example | No steps on the line yet · Give Nour a step on the Line | None now | Member | Edit';
  - the live region says 'Nour joined Sufra.'

sections.name: Channels: ways to reach clients
sections.content:
- **H2:** 'Channels'.
- **Description:** 'How Sufra’s line reaches its clients. Every message goes out in Sufra’s name.'
- **H3:** 'Ways to reach clients'.

**Rows:**
- Email · On. 'From “Sufra” · replies go to orders@sufra.example · every email ends with Runs on Iqaa'. Action: Edit.
- WhatsApp · Not connected. 'Messages would come from Sufra’s own WhatsApp Business number, under Sufra’s name and mark. Iqaa is not in the conversation.' Action: 'Connect WhatsApp' (.btn).
- SMS · Not connected. 'For clients with neither email nor WhatsApp.' Action: 'Connect SMS' (.btn).

States are plain words: 'On' in ink at 700, 'Not connected' in n700. There are no chips and no switches.

sections.name: Channels: messages on the line
sections.content:
**H3 'Messages on the line'.**

Caption: 'The steps of Sufra’s line (version 3) that send something, in the order a job meets them. Which way each one goes is part of the line: change it on the Line, then publish a new version.'

Six rows, each with its step's own stroke, a straight in ink:
1. Send the client a receipt: 'Request · to the client · by email'. Today: 'Sending now to Lina Saleh, since 09:20'.
2. Send the quote link: 'Quote · to the client · by email'. Today: '08:52 to Omar'.
3. Remind the client: 'Client approval · after a wait of two days · to the client · by email'. Its glyph is the lifted pen and dot of the wait, then the straight.
4. Remind the kitchen a day before: 'Prepare · to Salma, inside Iqaa'.
5. Send the arrival time: 'Deliver · to the client · by email'. Today: '09:05 to Yara'.
6. Send the invoice: 'Invoice · to the client · by email'. Today: 'Sending now to Karim'.

Under the list: 'Messages to the team arrive inside Iqaa, on Today. Sufra’s channels are for its clients.'

Rows with no known event today show nothing in that slot.
sections.interactions:
- Rows 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 are buttons with aria-pressed that choose the preview. The quote link is pressed first.
- Row 4 is plain text, because it has no preview for a client.
- 'change it on the Line' is a link to line.html.

sections.name: Channels: the preview
sections.content:
**H3 'What the client gets'.** An email frame:
- Header: the mark at 28 px (or the logo tile), the sender name, and 'to Omar, Darb Studio'.
- Subject at 18/24, 700: 'Your quote for Office lunch'.
- Body at 14/20: 'Hi Omar, your quote is ready. Approve it or ask for a change from this link; you don’t need an account.'
- A violet 'Open the quote' button (the client's own action) and sufra.iqaa.app/q/0030 in Fragment Mono.
- 'Order SFR-26-0030 · Mon 2 Nov, 12:30 · 18 people' at 13/20 in n700.
- Foot, on n50: the Runs on Iqaa badge and 'You receive this because Sufra is preparing your order.'

Caption under the frame: 'Filled from Office lunch (SFR-26-0030). Sent to Omar at 08:52 today.'

**Once WhatsApp is connected:**
- An 'Email · WhatsApp' switch appears: two buttons with aria-pressed, in the Map/Build switch's look.
- The WhatsApp view shows the same words as a chat: the mark cut to a 28 px circle, 'Sufra · Business account', and one white bubble holding the text, the link and the time.
- No Iqaa anywhere: the co-branding rule on system.html.
sections.interactions:
- The preview redraws when a message row is pressed, when the sender name or reply-to is typed or saved, and when the organization's name, mark or logo is saved.
- The region has aria-label 'Preview of the selected message'. It is not a live region; the pressed row is what gets announced.

sections.name: Organization: setting rows
sections.content:
- **H2:** 'Organization'.
- **Description:** 'Sufra’s name, address and mark, as its team and clients see them.'

**Rows:**
- **Name:** Sufra.
  - Hint: 'Clients see it on every message and link. About 17 letters fit on one line in the sidebar.'
  - Change: a text field, maxlength 28 (as in the identity book's generator). Under 2 characters: 'Name your organization.'
- **Address:** sufra.iqaa.app (Fragment Mono).
  - Hint: 'It is in every link already sent to clients, like sufra.iqaa.app/q/0030, so it stays when the name changes.'
  - No action.
- **Field:** Catering.
  - Hint: 'Chosen at sign-up. Sufra’s line started from the Catering template and is its own now; change it on the Line.'
  - No action.
- **Working hours:** Every day, 08:00 to 18:00 (times in Fragment Mono).
  - Hint: 'The team’s day on Today and Overview, and each order’s times, are drawn on these hours.'
  - Change: two type=time fields, Opens and Closes. Error: 'Closing time must come after opening time.'
- **Time zone:** Asia/Hebron · now 09:41.
  - Hint: 'Every time on every screen uses it.'
  - Change: a select of Asia/Hebron, Asia/Gaza, Asia/Jerusalem, Asia/Amman, Africa/Cairo, Europe/Istanbul, Asia/Riyadh, Asia/Dubai, Europe/London, UTC.
- **Clients read Sufra in:** English.
  - Hint: 'Messages and client links. Arabic and Turkish follow on the same rules.'
  - No action: only English exists.

sections.name: Organization: Sufra's mark
sections.content:
**H3 'Sufra’s mark'.**

**Choice:** a fieldset with legend 'Sufra signs with' and two radios: 'Its initial, signed from its line' (checked) and 'Its own logo'.

**The plate:** ink, 16 px radius, padding 16.
- The mark at 96 px (72 px on phones). 96 px is the largest size the product draws it, at sign-up.
- Beside it, the opening that colours it, in the tile's own palette:
  - a lilac loop: 'Reem logs the order · a person';
  - a white straight: 'Send the client a receipt · runs by itself'.
- Glyphs are 24 px, names 14/20 in white, kinds 13/18 in n300.

**Caption:** 'Sufra’s line opens with Reem logs the order, a person’s step, then Send the client a receipt, which runs by itself. So the S is written half lilac, half white. Publish a line that opens differently and the S is written again.' Then the link 'See the line'.

**Own logo:**
- 'Choose a logo file': a .btn label for input type=file, accept 'image/png,image/jpeg,image/svg+xml'.
- Hint: 'A square PNG, JPG or SVG, at least 192 px: twice the largest size Iqaa shows a mark. It stays in this browser tab; nothing is uploaded.'
- After a valid choice, the plate and every preview show the logo, followed by Cancel / 'Use this logo' (violet).
- While a logo is in use, the plate caption reads 'Sufra’s own logo, on a white tile the shape of the mark’s, so the sidebar keeps its outline.' and 'Remove the logo' is offered.
sections.interactions: - **Reading the file.** It goes through URL.createObjectURL into an only; an SVG is never inserted as markup. - **Checks:** - type: 'Use a PNG, JPG or SVG file.' - decoding: 'Iqaa couldn’t read this file. Try another.' - size, for PNG and JPG: 'This image is 120 × 120 px. Use one at least 192 px on each side.' - shape, a warning that does not block: 'This image is 600 × 200 px, 3 times wider than tall. In the 32 px square of the sidebar it would stand 8 px tall. A square version reads better.' - An SVG without a natural size skips the size and shape checks. - **Logo tile:** white, corner radius 22.37 % of its size (the mark tile's ratio), a 1 px n200 inset ring, the image contained with 12.5 % padding. - **Use this logo:** note 'Sufra’s logo is in use on this page.' with Undo. The sidebar mark becomes the 32 px logo tile. - **Remove the logo:** the initial comes back. Note 'Back to Sufra’s initial.' with Undo. - Switching the radio back to the initial while a logo is in use shows Cancel / 'Use the initial'. - **A name whose first letter the hand does not write** (for example سفرة): grammar.js sets the letter in type in the colour of the line's first step, and the caption adds 'Iqaa’s hand writes A to Z and 0 to 9 so far, so س is set in type until it is drawn.' - Object URLs are revoked once no state and no Undo note holds them. - The opening always comes from the published line (SUFRA.line(), version 3), never from a Build draft in sessionStorage.

sections.name: Organization: where it appears
sections.content:
**H3 'Where it appears'**, with two groups labelled at 13/18, 700, n700.

**Your team sees it:**
- Sidebar · 32 px, on the n100 desk: the mark, the name at 15/20, 700 in the true 136 px name box (a long name wraps here exactly as it would there), and sufra.iqaa.app at 12/16 in n600.
- Sign-in · 40 px, on white: the mark, the name and the address.

**Clients see it:**
- Quote page · 28 px: the mark and the name, as on the client screen in system.html.
- Email · 28 px: the header, and the Runs on Iqaa foot.
- WhatsApp · 28 px, cut to a circle: the mark, 'Sufra' and 'Business account'. Until WhatsApp is connected, this snippet is drawn in n600 with 'When WhatsApp is connected'.

Each snippet is a figure with its caption. The sizes are the ones the code and the identity book use: app.js 32, signin.js 40, parts.css 28.
sections.interactions:
- All five follow the typed name, the chosen logo, Save and Undo together.
- The snippets are not interactive: their content is aria-hidden, and the figure caption says what each one is.

sections.name: Billing
sections.content:
- **H2:** 'Billing'.
- **Description:** 'What Sufra pays for Iqaa. The invoices Sufra sends its own clients are made on the line, at Invoice.'

**Rows:**
- **Plan:** [PLAN] · [PRICE] a month. Hint: 'Iqaa’s plans and prices are not set yet, so they show in brackets.' No action.
- **What Sufra uses:** a dl with numbers in Fragment Mono:
  - 'People who sign in: 4, and 1 invited'
  - 'Orders opened: 1 so far in November · 12 in October'
  - 'Channels on: Email'
- **Invoices from Iqaa go to:** hala@sufra.example. Change opens an email field with sign-up's messages.
- **Name on Iqaa’s invoices:** Sufra · [ADDRESS], Ramallah. Change opens Name and Address.
- **Invoices from Iqaa:** 'None yet.' No action.

Billing has no strokes: nothing in it is a step of the line.
sections.interactions:
- Usage is live: sending, cancelling or accepting an invitation, and connecting a channel, change it at once.
- Notes: 'Invoices from Iqaa now go to …' with Undo.

sections.name: Viewing as a member
sections.content:
settings.html?as=reem, salma or yusuf.
- settings.js sets the sidebar's data-me-av, data-me-name and data-me-role before app.js runs, as Today does, so the sidebar's counts follow the viewer.
- Every value is plain text: no Invite, Edit, Change, Connect, radios or file input.
- Team keeps the waiting links. The invitation row has no actions.
- Billing's nav summary reads 'Owners only'. Its area holds only the Lock icon and 'Only owners see billing. Ask Hala if something here needs changing.'
sections.interactions: Routes, previews and search results are the same as for the owner.

sections.name: Prototype footer and what can be changed
sections.content:
**Footer**, in order:
- the Runs on Iqaa sign-off;
- 'Prototype: see Settings as Hala, an owner · Reem, a member. Changes last until you leave the page.', followed by the button 'Let Nour accept her invitation';
- the shell's own line: 'Prototype screen, part of the Iqaa identity. Nothing is sent or saved.'

**Can be changed** (page memory, each with Undo):
- Team: invite someone, send again, cancel an invitation, let Nour accept, change what someone does, set Owner or Member, remove someone with no steps and no waiting jobs.
- Channels: sender name, reply-to, connect or disconnect WhatsApp and SMS, which message is previewed.
- Organization: name, working hours, time zone, initial or own logo.
- Billing: where invoices go, the name on them.

**Fixed**, with the reason shown: address, field, client language, the Runs on Iqaa line, plan and price, invoices from Iqaa, who does each step, and which way each message goes (both set on the Line).
sections.interactions:
- A reload resets everything to sufra.js.
- Only this page's sidebar follows a rename or a logo; other screens keep Sufra.

identity_details: **Team strips.** Each person row carries Today's metro strip without the train, with that person's stations ringed violet. Reem is ringed at Request and Quote; Hala at Buy materials and, on the branch dip, Wholesale order. It is the drawing Today already uses for 'your station', now saying where each person holds the line.

**Their own strokes.** A person's steps are listed in their own strokes: a loop for what they do, an open arch for what waits for them ('Approves Watar’s draft of the quote'). The removal guard reads from the same list, so the grammar is the reason the Remove button is locked.

**Invitation as a line.** An invitation is drawn as a short line: an ink straight (Iqaa sent the link, a step that runs by itself), then a violet arch (it waits for Nour). When she accepts, the pen rewrites it as a straight and a loop, a quarter beat a stroke: the approval moment from the Motion page.
**Invited avatar.** An invited person's avatar is an empty ring with a 1.5 px n500 border, not dashed. The dashed grey pen stays reserved for things that are not real yet.

**Not saved yet.** An unsaved change is a person's step not done yet. So it is drawn the way Today and the order page draw what is still yours: a dashed grey loop, at 16 px, beside the words 'Not saved yet'. Saving writes a solid violet loop into the note in a quarter beat: a person's hand took it. It is a loop and not an arch, because a dashed grey arch is how Watar's drafts look, and these changes are the person's own.

**Messages on the line.** The line's messages are listed as its straight ink strokes, in line order. The client reminder carries the lifted pen and dot of its two-day wait before its straight, exactly as the Line draws it.

**The mark explained.** The mark is explained by the line that writes it. The S sits at 96 px on an ink plate beside the opening, drawn in the tile's own palette: a lilac loop for 'Reem logs the order', a white straight for 'Send the client a receipt'. The sentence under it is generated from IQ.lead.
- Renaming writes a new initial with the pen only when the first letter changes.
- A letter the hand does not draw yet is set in type, as decisions.html requires.

**True sizes.** 'Where it appears' shows the mark only where and at the size it is really used: sidebar 32, sign-in 40, quote page 28, email 28, WhatsApp 28 cut to a circle. There is no browser-tab context, because the app pages use Iqaa's own favicon.

**The organization leads.** The email preview ends with the Runs on Iqaa badge, and the email editor says that line cannot be changed. The WhatsApp preview has no Iqaa in it at all. This is the co-branding rule from system.html.

**Violet only for people.** Avatars, rings, arches, loops, and the buttons a person presses (Invite someone, Save, Send the invitation, Connect, Use this logo) are violet. Channel states are words, not violet switches: the guidelines' 'a violet switch says a person did it'.
**Fragment Mono** for sufra.iqaa.app, client links such as sufra.iqaa.app/q/0030, order codes, times (08:52, 08:00), counts and phone numbers. Atkinson for names, emails and every sentence.
**Billing has no strokes:** nothing in it is a step of the line. The only rounded grounds on the page are the previews and the plate, because they show other places.
computations: **Line and helpers.** line = SUFRA.line() (the published version 3); J = JOBS.on(line); live = SUFRA.jobs.filter(j => !j.finished); isPerson(kind) = kind is 'held' or 'struck'.

**A person's steps.** Every step in line.stations[].steps and in each branch route's stations[].steps with isPerson(kind) and who === name, in route order, each with its station.
- Reem: Request 'Reem logs the order' (struck); Quote 'Watar drafts the quote' (held); Quote 'Reem checks the prices' (struck).
- Hala: Buy materials 'Buy the materials'; Wholesale order 'Hala orders from the wholesaler'.
- Salma: Prepare 'Salma prepares'.
- Yusuf: Deliver 'Yusuf delivers'.

**Step label from a person's side.** /^Watar drafts (.+)$/ becomes 'Approves Watar’s draft of $1' (the same rule as today.js doneName). Any other held step becomes 'Approves: {name}'. A struck step keeps its name.

**Team order.** Sort by the smallest station index among the person's steps. A main station counts as its index; a branch station counts as the index of route.from + 0.5. Result: Reem 0, Hala 2.5, Salma 4, Yusuf 5. Someone with no steps sorts last.
**Line words in a person row.** The unique station names in order, joined with ', ', plus ' · {n} step(s)'. Example: 'Request, Quote · 3 steps'.

**Waiting now.** live jobs where J.stepOf(j) is a person step whose who === name. This gives Reem SFR-26-0031, 0034 and 0032; Hala 0029; Salma 0028; Yusuf 0027. Together they equal Overview's 'With the team' (6).
**Coverage sentence.** Over all person steps: who in team names gives 7; who === 'The client' gives 1; anything else would read '{n} with no one', which cannot happen in the demo.
**Removal guard.** Blocked when steps.length > 0 or waiting.length > 0. The reason text is built from the counts and station names, always using the name, never a pronoun.

**reach(ring)** in jobs.js reuses GAP 22, PAD 9, Y 9 and xAt.
- It draws the 150 × 26 track and every main station, with class 'me' where ring(st) is true.
- For each branch that has a ringed station, it draws the dip 'M{a} 9L{a+8} 20H{b-8}L{b} 9' (class 'tr br'), where a and b are xAt of route.from and route.to.
- Each ringed branch station is a circle at a + (b - a)(j + 1)/(n + 1), y 20. For Hala's Wholesale order that is (75, 20).
- It draws no train.

**Invitation dates.** sent '2026-10-30T16:20' is formatted with order.js's fmt as 'Fri 30 Oct, 16:20'. The link expires 7 days after the sent date, formatted 'Fri 6 Nov' (weekday short, day, month short, comma removed). A new invite or a 'Send again' on 1 Nov expires 'Sun 8 Nov'.

**Nav summaries.**
- Team: '{people} people · {invites} invited'. The second part is dropped when there are no invites.
- Channels: the connected channels give 'Sends by email' / 'Email and WhatsApp on' / 'Email, WhatsApp and SMS on'.
- Organization: a 20 px mark plus the address.
- Billing: '{plan} · {price} a month', or 'Owners only' for a member.

**Message rows.** The steps of the main stations, in order (the branch has none), with kind 'run' and who 'Send' or 'Remind'. There are 6. For each row:
- 'to' and 'by' come from SUFRA.messages.
- If the previous step in the same station is 'rest', the row shows the rest glyph and 'after a wait of {who.toLowerCase()}', which gives 'two days'.
- For the team row, the person is who does the station's struck step: Salma.

**Today's events per message.**
- Running now: a live job whose J.stepOf(j) is that step. These are SFR-26-0035 (receipt) and SFR-26-0026 (invoice). A done entry for that job today adds 'since {time}', which gives 09:20 for Lina.
- Sent today: for each SUFRA.done entry d, take the job's route steps flattened through J.route(job). i0 is the index of the step named d.step; i1 is the index of the job's current step. Every 'run' step strictly between them was sent at d.time to job.client. Result: 'Send the quote link' 08:52 to Omar (0030), and 'Send the arrival time' 09:05 to Yara (0027).

**Preview job per message.** First the latest sent-today job; otherwise the running-now job; otherwise the live job with the fewest steps to reach the message, counting through J.stepOf and J.ahead.
- Receipt: 0035 Lina.
- Quote link: 0030 Omar.
- Remind the client: 0030 Omar, one step away after its wait. 0033 Rania is two away.
- Arrival time: 0027 Yara.
- Invoice: 0026 Karim.

Captions: 'Sent to Omar at 08:52 today.', 'Sending to Lina Saleh now.', or 'The next job to reach this step.'

**Template fill.**
- {org}: the saved organization name, or the typed draft while the Name editor is open.
- {client}: the first word of job.client.
- {title}, {people}, {due}: from the job.
- {time}: the part of due after the comma.
- {link}: 'sufra.iqaa.app/q/' + the last four digits of the code (the same rule as order.js).
- {deliverer}: who does the struck step at Deliver, which is Yusuf.
- 'to' line: the client, plus ', {of}' unless 'of' starts with 'a ' ('a private order').
- Order line: 'Order {code} · {due} · {people} people'.

**Mark and its opening.** blocks = line.stations mapped to { name, steps: kinds }. The opening is IQ.lead(blocks.map(b => b.steps), 3), which gives [['struck', 'run']]. The plate labels come from the first station's step names. grammar.js gives each step an equal share of the letter: lilac (#C9A4FF) for a person, white for a run.

**Colour words in the caption.** For an opening of n steps with p person steps:
- n = 2, p = 1: 'half lilac, half white'.
- p = n: 'in lilac'.
- p = 0: 'in white'.
- n = 3: thirds, for example 'two thirds lilac, one third white'.
**Initial.** name.trim().charAt(0).toUpperCase(). If window.IQAA.letters has that key (A to Z, 0 to 9), the hand writes it; otherwise it is set in type, and the caption adds the hand note.

**Sidebar fit hint.** The name box measures 136 px at 1440. Atkinson 15 px bold averages 7.87 px per lowercase letter (measured), so about 17 letters fit on a line. The Sidebar snippet renders at the same 136 px, so wrapping is shown, not computed.

**Logo checks.**
- Type is one of image/png, image/jpeg or image/svg+xml.
- The file must decode through an Image() from a blob URL.
- For PNG and JPG, min(naturalWidth, naturalHeight) must be at least 192 (2 × the 96 px sign-up mark).
- Ratio r = max / min. When r > 1.25, warn: the height in the sidebar = round(24 / r) px. 24 px is the 32 px tile minus 12.5 % padding on each side, so 600 × 200 gives 8 px.
- An SVG with naturalWidth 0 skips size and ratio.

**Time zone 'now'.** demo instant = Date.UTC(2026, 10, 1, 7, 41), which is 09:41 in Asia/Hebron at GMT+2 per tzdata 2026e, plus the time since the page loaded. It is formatted with Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-GB', { timeZone, hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit' }). Measured: Hebron, Gaza, Jerusalem and Cairo 09:41; Amman, Istanbul and Riyadh 10:41; Dubai 11:41; London and UTC 07:41.

**Usage.** Group SUFRA.jobs[].opened by month: 2026-10 gives 12 (SFR-26-0023 to 0034); 2026-11 gives 1 (SFR-26-0035, today at 09:12). People who sign in = state.people.length (4), plus state.invites.length (1). Channels on = the names of the connected channels.
**Demo clock.** SUFRA.now ('09:41') plus whole minutes since the page loaded, as today.js does. It is used for 'now' in the Time zone row.
states: **Owner, default (desktop).** The page opens on Team. Nothing is pending, no note shows, and the four nav summaries are visible. The only violet is the people's avatars, rings and arches, Nour's arch and 'Invite someone'.
**Phone list view** (settings.html at under 900 px). The head and four area rows with their summaries.
**Phone area view.** '← Settings', then the area full screen.
**Medium width** (content under 960 px). The nav is a row of four links above the area, with no summaries.
**Editor open, unchanged.** No marker. The other areas are untouched.
**Editor with changes.** 'Not saved yet' with a dashed grey loop shows in the editor and in the nav summary. It survives visiting another area. Leaving the page triggers the browser's own prompt.

**Validation error.**
- The message sits under its field (.err), aria-invalid is set and focus moves to the first invalid field.
- Examples: 'Name your organization.', 'Write the number with its country code, starting with +.', 'Closing time must come after opening time.', 'reem@sufra.example already belongs to Reem.'

**Saved.** The editor closes, and the note in the row starts with a violet loop the pen writes. Summaries update. Undo is available for 8 s, and the timer pauses while the pointer or focus is inside the note.
**Taken back (Undo).** The state from before the change returns. Focus goes to the row's action, and the live region says 'Taken back.'
**Remove blocked** (Reem, Salma, Yusuf). The button is aria-disabled and its reason is written beside it, with a link to the Line.
**Remove allowed** (Nour after she joins). A placeholder row with 'Nour is no longer on Sufra’s team.' and Undo.

**Invitations.**
- Pending: Nour, straight and arch.
- Sent: a new row the pen writes.
- Sent again.
- Cancelled: a placeholder row with Undo.
- Accepted: straight and loop; the row moves to People with 'No steps on the line yet'.
- None: 'No invitations out.'

**WhatsApp and SMS.**
- Not connected.
- Connect form open.
- Invalid number.
- Connected (prototype: 'nothing is sent'): the Channels summary updates and the preview gains the WhatsApp view.
- Disconnected, with Undo.

**Preview.** One state for each of the five client messages, each with its caption: sent at a time, sending now, or the next job to reach the step. Email view only until WhatsApp is connected; then Email and WhatsApp.

**Name.**
- Same initial: the mark keeps its S.
- New initial: the pen writes it in the preview, then in the sidebar on Save.
- An initial the hand does not write (Arabic or Ö): set in type, plus the hand note.
- Under 2 characters: an error.
- A long name: wraps to two lines in the Sidebar snippet, as it would in the real sidebar.

**Logo.**
- Choosing.
- Wrong type.
- Unreadable.
- Too small (blocked).
- Wide (a warning with the height in pixels, still allowed).
- In use: the sidebar mark becomes the logo tile.
- Removed: back to the initial.
- An SVG without a natural size: no size or shape check.
**Member view** (?as=reem). Read-only text everywhere. The member lead is shown, and Billing is locked with 'Owners only'.
**Deep link** to an area: that area opens with its H2 focused. An unknown hash opens the default view. #main keeps the current view.
**Reduced motion.** The pen does not write and the page does not scroll smoothly. Every change appears at once, and notes keep their 8 s and Undo.
**No JavaScript.** The head, the nav links and the area headings with their descriptions (a prototype limit).

accessibility: **Headings and landmarks.** One H1 'Settings' (visually hidden in a phone area view), one H2 per area, H3 for groups. Each area is a <section aria-labelledby> pointing at its H2. Hidden areas use the hidden attribute, so they are out of the accessibility tree.
**Settings nav.** nav aria-label 'Settings areas', with aria-current='page' on the open area. Each link's name includes its summary, for example 'Team, 4 people, 1 invited' or 'Team, not saved yet'.
**Route changes.** Every route change focuses the area's H2 (tabindex -1, preventScroll) and updates document.title. The list view focuses the H1. Searching to an area lands the same way.

**Editors.** Actions are buttons with aria-expanded and aria-controls, plus visually hidden objects ('Change the name', 'Edit Reem'). - Forms are novalidate, and every field has a visible label. - Hints and errors are linked with aria-describedby, and invalid fields get aria-invalid. - Save moves focus to the first invalid field. - Escape cancels and returns focus to the action that opened the editor.

**Notes.** Each note is visible in its row, and one page-level polite live region (.sr) announces saved, taken back, joined and connected. Focus is never moved by a note.
- The 8 s timer pauses while the pointer or focus is inside the note (WCAG 2.2.1).
- Undo is a real button right after the text.
**Disabled actions.** A disabled Remove uses aria-disabled, not the disabled attribute, so it stays focusable, and its written reason is linked with aria-describedby.

**Choices and files.** Role and the mark choice are radios in fieldsets with legends. The file input has a visible label (the 'Choose a logo file' button). The chosen file's pixel size is given in text. The preview image's alt is 'Sufra’s logo, preview'.

**Previews.** Message rows are buttons with aria-pressed. The preview region has aria-label 'Preview of the selected message'. The 'Where it appears' snippets are aria-hidden inside figures whose captions name them.
**Glyphs and strips.** Every glyph, strip and invitation line is aria-hidden, with the same facts in words beside it. A state is never told by shape or colour alone.
**Targets.** At least 44 px everywhere: text buttons are 44 px tall, nav items 56, list rows 72, and the phone back link 44. .btn.small (36 px) is not used.

**Contrast** (measured):
- Text is ink or n800. Secondary text is n700: 8.16:1 on white, 7.46:1 on n50.
- Nothing fainter than n600 (5.65:1).
- n500 is used only for graphics (3.95:1, over the 3:1 rule).
- Violet as text only on white (4.94:1).
- On the plate: lilac on ink 8.51:1, n300 on ink 8.40:1.
**Reduced motion.** prefers-reduced-motion stops the pen and smooth scrolling. Every change is instant and every note is kept.

rejected: **A's single long page with a scroll-spy index.** Four forms on about 3,100 px is busier than one area at a time. The index's live summaries survive as the persistent local nav.

**A's per-part forms**, with changed-field dashed rules, sticky save bars, blocked and confirm states in the bar, Ctrl/Cmd S, and scroll padding for the bars. Atomic row edits with Undo do the same job with the app's own pattern (Line notes, Today's take-back). On a phone, A's stacked bars would cover about 176 of 812 px.
**B's separate home ledger.** It costs a click on every desktop visit. Its glance moves into the local nav, and on phones the nav list is the home.

**A's WhatsApp on, with three steps sending by it.** It contradicts Build's seed (every Send step 'By: Email') and would show a live integration. WhatsApp and SMS start not connected, and Connect says nothing is sent.
**A's 'Reem’s steps go to Hala on removal'.** It would edit the versioned line from Settings. B's guard keeps the Line as the only place that changes who does a step.
**B's Manager role and its role table.** Two roles match PRODUCT.md's two kinds of users, and the radio descriptions carry the facts.
**B's quiet hours, WhatsApp fallback switch, working-day toggles and order-code letters.** They are invented product rules beyond the brief; they were cut so the core gets depth.
**A's 'On quotes and invoices' group** (legal name, tax number and phone, all in brackets). A block of placeholders that reads unfinished.
**B's paid invoices with [AMOUNT], the next-invoice date and the Invoicing pack line, and A's 'Pilot' plan name.** These are invented billing facts. 'None yet' and [PLAN] are used instead.
**B's 'Send a test to Hala' drawn in the dashed grey pen.** A test email to yourself would really be sent, while the grammar's test sends nothing. Mixing the two blurs the rule.

**B's browser-tab context in 'Where it appears'.** App pages use Iqaa's favicon, so it would be untrue. B's 28 / 40 px sizes for email and WhatsApp were replaced by the sizes the code and the book use.

**Confirm dialogs for removing a person, cancelling an invitation or disconnecting a channel.** The Line removes a station with an Undo note and keeps confirms for publishing. Settings follows that convention.
**Channel on/off switches, and A's red-snap consequences for turning Email off.** No step can lose its only channel here. Which way a message goes is set on the Line.
**Auto-dismissing the saved state after one bar (2400 ms).** --m-bar caps animation, not reading time. Notes stay 8 s as on the Line and pause on hover or focus.
**Supporting an organization made at sign-up** (sessionStorage 'iqaa-org'). Overview and Orders don't honour it either; it is out of scope for this pass.
**Settings as a phone tab.** The 359 px bar holds five 64 px items (measured); the organization menu and search are the ways in.
**A local copy of lead() or of the strip in settings.js.** Both are exported or added in grammar.js and jobs.js, so the mark, its sentence and every strip share one rule.
